title: ReviewPlane review domain, version 1
description: Single source for the durable review objects of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md sections 14 to 20 and the request bodies and audit events that carry them (docs/API.md sections 12 to 15, docs/EVENTS.md section 7). The review is the system of record (ADR-0004) and annotation geometry is stored apart from the original evidence (ADR-0006), so the shapes here are shared by the HTTP API today and by the MCP tools of docs/MCP_SPEC.md sections 7.6 and 7.7 next. TypeScript models, validators and canonical encoders are generated from this file; hand-maintained equivalents in apps/server or apps/web are a review failure.

channels.review: Review lifecycle: creation, naming and status.
channels.finding: Finding lifecycle, including annotation of a finding.
channels.inbox: Durable delivery of assigned work to a human or an agent session (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 21).
channels.command: Request bodies of the human and agent write API.
channels.refusal: Stable refusals carried back to a caller.

review.created.description: A review exists. It is the durable record the rest of the loop hangs from (ADR-0004), so the event carries the captured source context that makes the review reproducible later.

review.named.description: A review received or changed its human-facing title and project-scoped slug. Separate from review.created because the slug is a mutable alias (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3) whose history has to be readable.

review.status_changed.description: A review moved between the statuses of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14. The actor type is explicit because an agent may not move a review to ACCEPTED.

finding.created.description: A finding exists inside a review, with the captured context of docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 9 that makes it reproducible.

finding.annotated.description: An annotation was recorded against a finding's screenshot. The geometry is normalised to the artefact content rectangle and is stored apart from the original bytes (ADR-0006).

finding.status_changed.description: A finding moved between the statuses of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15. A human-authored finding reaching RESOLVED requires a human actor; the denial is a domain rule, not a presentation rule.

review.claimed.description: An agent session took a review to work on. It is separate from review.status_changed because assignment and lifecycle are different facts: a claim says who is working, and the status says what stage the work is at.

finding.claimed.description: An agent session took one finding. Claims are recorded per finding so a human can see which unit of work an agent is on rather than only that it is busy.

finding.comment_added.description: A comment was appended to a finding (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 18). Comments are append-only and the author type is always explicit, because a reader must be able to tell an agent's note from a human's.

finding.verification_submitted.description: An agent submitted a claim with evidence that a finding is resolved (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). It is the event that carries the before-and-after evidence a human then judges; submitting it accepts nothing.

finding.verification_accepted.description: A human accepted a specific claim. It sits beside finding.resolved rather than instead of it: the disposition says the finding is closed, this says which evidence closed it, and only the second survives an agent submitting different evidence afterwards (ADR-0035).

finding.verification_rejected.description: A human rejected a specific claim and sent the finding back. The rejected record is retained with status rejected rather than deleted, so the history of what has been claimed before and failed stays readable (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19).

review.completion_evaluated.description: An agent asked the completion gate whether its work was done, and was told (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.8). It records an evaluation and never a change: no review, finding or verification moves because of it. It exists because the moment an agent believes it has finished is a moment worth being able to reconstruct — including the case where it was told blocked_pending_review and what it did next.

review.assigned.description: A review was assigned to a human or to an agent session. Assignment is separate from review.claimed because one is a human directing work and the other is a worker taking it, and an auditor needs to tell the two apart.

review.accepted.description: A human accepted a review. The payload names the human who decided and the findings the decision rested on, because acceptance is the authority boundary of AGENTS.md and an audit trail that only recorded the status would not say who crossed it.

review.reopened.description: An accepted review was reopened. docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14 makes an accepted review immutable, so reopening is recorded as an explicit event rather than as an ordinary status change; prior findings, evidence and comments are retained.

review.archived.description: A review was archived. Archival is not deletion: the findings, evidence and events all outlive it, which is why the event records the status it was archived from.

review.comment_added.description: A comment was appended to a review itself rather than to one of its findings (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 18). It is a separate type from finding.comment_added so that a consumer filtering a finding's timeline does not have to inspect a payload to know whether an event belongs to it.

finding.resolved.description: A human accepted a finding as resolved, or explicitly waived it as WONT_FIX or DUPLICATE. It is separate from finding.status_changed because a final disposition is the decision the authority rule of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15 reserves to a human, and it must be findable in the stream without matching on a status value.

finding.reopened.description: A human reopened a finding that had been resolved or waived. Prior verification history is retained rather than discarded, so the event carries how many verifications already exist.

review.status_change_denied.description: A principal asked for a review transition it may not make, and was refused. It is recorded because the refusal is the authority boundary of AGENTS.md holding: an attempt to accept a review with agent credentials must leave a trail, and a rolled-back transaction leaves none.

finding.status_change_denied.description: A principal asked for a finding transition it may not make, and was refused. The Stage 1 exit criterion is that an agent cannot finally accept a human-authored finding and that the attempt is audited; this is the audit half, and it is written outside the refused transaction because that transaction never commits.

inbox_item.created.description: Work was delivered to a recipient's inbox (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 21). It is written in the same transaction as the assignment or the reopen that caused it, so a delivery that was recorded is a delivery that happened.

inbox_item.acknowledged.description: A recipient acknowledged receipt. It is deliberately a different event from inbox_item.completed: acknowledgement says the work was seen and never that it was done, and an auditor asking which of the two happened must not have to infer it.

inbox_item.completed.description: The work an inbox item delivered was recorded complete.

inbox_item.dismissed.description: A human dismissed an inbox item without completing the work. It is audited because dismissing delivered feedback is a decision somebody made, and docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 21 lists dismissed as a status a record can hold.

inbox_item.expired.description: An inbox item passed its expiry without being acted on. It is a conclusion the control plane draws rather than an act a recipient performed.

artefact.upload_started.description: An upload intent was recorded. The artefact is not evidence yet: it becomes available only after the control plane verifies size and digest (docs/API.md section 15).

artefact.upload_completed.description: The stored bytes were verified against the declared size and digest and the artefact became available.

artefact.upload_failed.description: Verification failed. The artefact stays unavailable and the reason is recorded, because a finding without verified evidence must remain visibly without evidence.

artefact.access_granted.description: A short-lived, subject-scoped grant was minted for one artefact (docs/SECURITY.md section 13, ADR-0012, ADR-0019). Reading evidence is an audited access, not an anonymous fetch.

artefact.deleted.description: An artefact was deleted. The metadata row survives so the identifier still resolves in the audit trail, and the payload says whether the stored object was actually removed — it is not, when another live artefact shares the same content-addressed key.

artefact.thumbnail_generated.description: The durable thumbnail job finished for an image artefact. It is recorded for every outcome, including the ones that produced no thumbnail, so a viewer can say which of not-yet, not-possible and failed applies.

screenshot.captured.description: A verified screenshot artefact exists, with the content rectangle that annotation geometry is normalised against.

review_update_request.description: Body of PATCH /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId. Carries expected_version, so a concurrent edit is refused rather than silently overwritten (docs/API.md section 13, docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 11).

finding_create_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId/findings. The captured context of docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 9 is required, because a finding without it is not reproducible later.

finding_update_request.description: Body of PATCH /api/v1/findings/:findingId, including the status transition an agent may or may not perform.

annotation_create_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/findings/:findingId/annotations. Geometry outside 0 to 1 is refused here rather than clamped, so a coordinate-frame mistake surfaces at the boundary instead of becoming a misplaced overlay.

annotation_update_request.description: Body of PATCH /api/v1/annotations/:annotationId. It carries expected_revision, so an edit against a revision another writer has already superseded is refused rather than silently applied over it (docs/API.md section 14).

artefact_upload_intent_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/artefacts/uploads (docs/API.md section 15). Every declared value is verified against the stored bytes before the artefact becomes evidence.

artefact_upload_completion_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/artefacts/:artefactId/complete. The observed digest is compared with the declared one and with the digest of the bytes read back out of the store.

artefact_upload_intent_response.description: Where to send the bytes: the proxied path under the filesystem driver, or a short-lived presigned URL under the s3 driver.

artefact_resource.description: The artefact:// and screenshot:// resource representation of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 8, carrying the trust label every browser-derived value must reach an agent with.

artefact_store_status.description: Artefact-store driver, reachability and storage use, as reviewplane status reports them (docs/OPERATIONS.md section 3).

review_assign_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId/assign. Exactly one of a user or an agent session is named; assigning to both would leave the question of who owns the work unanswered.

review_transition_request.description: Body of the review lifecycle routes of docs/API.md section 12: request-review, accept, reopen and archive. Each carries expected_version, because each is a write to a record two principals may be holding.

finding_claim_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/findings/:findingId/claim. The claim uses the same optimistic-concurrency mechanism as any other write, so a human and an agent claiming at once produce one claim and one VERSION_CONFLICT.

finding_transition_request.description: Body of the human-only finding disposition routes of docs/API.md section 13: accept, reopen and wont-fix. They are human-only in the domain layer, so an agent credential reaching one is refused with AUTHORISATION_DENIED and audited.

verification_review.description: Response of GET /api/v1/findings/:findingId/verifications/:verificationId (docs/API.md section 13). It is the shape a human reviewer decides from: one named claim, the assurance split of docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 13, and whether the claim is still the one a decision may be taken on.

verification_create_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/findings/:findingId/verifications (docs/API.md section 13). It carries no submitted_by and no status: the submitter is the authenticated actor and the status is always submitted, so neither an attribution nor a decision is a field a caller may set.

comment_create_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId/comments and POST /api/v1/findings/:findingId/comments. It carries no author: attribution is derived from the authenticated actor and is not a field a caller may set (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 18).

comment_update_request.description: Body of PATCH /api/v1/comments/:commentId. An edit appends a new revision and retains the previous one; nothing overwrites a comment in place.

domain_error.description: The docs/API.md section 5 error object, carrying the stable code of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12.

frame_too_large.description: The encoded event exceeded its byte bound. Detected on the raw bytes before deserialisation.

malformed_json.description: The event was not well-formed JSON, or was truncated.

unsupported_schema_version.description: schema_version was absent, not an integer, or not a version this build accepts (docs/EVENTS.md section 2).

unknown_message_type.description: type was absent or not a version 1 event type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored.

payload_too_large.description: The payload exceeded the byte bound declared for its event type.

schema_violation.description: The event parsed but did not satisfy the schema for its type.

geometry_by_annotation_type.description: Which geometry members each annotation type uses, in the form type:version:required[:optional]. The schema bounds every member to 0 to 1; this list fixes which of them a type requires, which it may carry and which it forbids, and is enforced by checkGeometryForType in src/annotation-geometry.ts because JSON Schema cannot condition a nested object on a sibling property. rectangle and ellipse are a box that may be rotated; point and numbered_marker are a position; arrow is a tail plus a head; freehand is a box plus the sampled path inside it. The second field is the geometry version of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16, held per type rather than per document so that adding a member to one shape does not renumber the others (ADR-0032); it is stored on every annotation so a reader knows which member list a stored geometry was written against.

reference_frame.description: The frame normalised geometry is expressed in. It is the artefact content rectangle of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16: the full intrinsic pixel extent of the stored image, origin at its top-left. It is deliberately neither the viewport, nor the element, nor the rendered element box, because those three differ under zoom, container resize and a device-pixel-ratio change while the content rectangle does not.

review_status_transitions.description: The review lifecycle of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14 as data, one entry per legal transition, in the form from:to:actor_types. The third field is the authority column: which actor types may request that transition. Absence from this list means refused — a status machine with an implicit "anything else is fine" branch is not a status machine. The list is the single source the control plane, the MCP layer and the web application all read (ADR-0024), so a permitted action is never computed twice from two copies of the rule. An agent may reach exactly three of the nine statuses: ASSIGNED by claiming, IN_PROGRESS and AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW by working. ACCEPTED is human-only, which is the authority boundary of AGENTS.md. ACCEPTED to CHANGES_REQUESTED is the reopen of section 14, an explicit and audited exception to the immutability of an accepted review.

finding_status_transitions.description: The finding lifecycle of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15 as data, one entry per legal transition, in the form from:to:actor_types. The third field is the authority column of the same section, and the entries naming agent_session are exactly the six transitions of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.7 and nothing else. The list stops at AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW for an agent, which is the product invariant of AGENTS.md expressed as data: an agent submits work for review and a human decides. RESOLVED, WONT_FIX and DUPLICATE are final dispositions and are human-only whoever authored the finding, because Stage 1 enables no policy that would auto-resolve an agent-authored one.

final_finding_dispositions.description: The finding statuses that finally dispose of the reported problem. Reaching one is a decision about whether the problem was real, which docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15 reserves to a human for a human-authored finding and which Stage 1 reserves to a human for an agent-authored one too, because no project policy exists yet to permit auto-resolution. Review acceptance treats them as the statuses a finding must have reached before the review may be accepted.

active_review_statuses.description: The review statuses whose slug still reserves the project-scoped name of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14. A withdrawn review releases its name and an accepted one keeps it, because an agent told to work on bugs-on-homepage must never face two candidates.

immutable_review_statuses.description: The review statuses in which a review is closed to ordinary edits (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14). Comments, archival metadata and an explicit reopen remain available; everything else is refused with POLICY_DENIED rather than silently dropped.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, with a mandatory trailing Z.

slug.description: Project-scoped human alias for a review, for example bugs-on-homepage. Unique among active reviews of one project and not across projects (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14). A slug is a mutable alias and never an identity.

title_text.description: Human-authored title. Rendered as text and never as markup.

body_text.description: Human-authored or agent-authored prose: a description, instruction, acceptance criterion or resolution note. Rendered as text and never as markup.

reason_text.description: Short operator-facing explanation. Never carries credentials (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

captured_url.description: Absolute URL the finding was captured at. Page-derived and therefore untrusted (ADR-0010): bounded in length and character class, rendered as text, never executed.

branch_name.description: Version-control branch the capture was taken from. Recorded so a review can be judged stale later (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 24), which Stage 0 does not yet compute.

commit_sha.description: Version-control commit the capture was taken from.

sha256_hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, as verified by the control plane.

storage_key.description: Content-addressed artefact key. Derived from the digest the server computed and never from a user-entered name (ADR-0012, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2), which is why path traversal through it is impossible rather than filtered.

media_type.description: Media type of stored artefact bytes, bounded to the types the artefact store accepts. text/html is the DOM snapshot of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 20 and is the one active type in the list: it is stored, but it is never served inline under the control-plane origin, only as an attachment, and artefact_disposition says so on every record (docs/SECURITY.md section 13). image/svg+xml is deliberately absent — no Stage 1 kind needs it, so an SVG is refused on upload rather than stored and then held back at the reader.

artefact_disposition.description: How the control plane serves these bytes. inline is what an img element needs and is used only for the inert image types; attachment is what active markup gets, so that a document which could execute is downloaded rather than rendered under the control-plane origin (docs/SECURITY.md section 13, docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 17). It is a property of the media type rather than a caller's choice, and a caller cannot ask for inline.

artefact_storage_driver.description: Artefact storage driver in use (ADR-0012). filesystem is the default and requires no additional service; s3 targets any S3-compatible endpoint. The name appears in configuration and in status output, and nowhere in the domain: no caller may choose it and no artefact record depends on it.

thumbnail_state.description: What became of the derived thumbnail for an image artefact. It is recorded rather than inferred, because 'no thumbnail row' is ambiguous between not yet generated, not generatable and failed — and docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 18 forbids a viewer that cannot say which. unsupported is an honest terminal outcome: the Stage 1 thumbnailer decodes PNG only, so a JPEG source is recorded as unsupported instead of retried forever.

version_number.description: Optimistic-concurrency version. Every accepted mutation increments it by one; a caller presenting a stale value is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT (docs/API.md section 13, docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 11).

sequence_number.description: Position in the project event stream. Monotonic within a project and not globally (docs/EVENTS.md section 3).

marker_number.description: Ordinal shown inside a numbered marker, so the annotation list and the overlay name the same mark (docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 19).

byte_size.description: Byte length the control plane verified.

pixel_extent.description: A dimension in device pixels of the stored image.

css_pixel_offset.description: An offset in CSS pixels within the captured document.

normalised_coordinate.description: A coordinate normalised to the artefact content rectangle, inclusive of both bounds (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16). A value outside the range is a coordinate-frame mistake and MUST be refused rather than clamped, because clamping turns a wrong frame into a plausible-looking overlay.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio of the capture. It scales the raster and never the normalised geometry, which is why an annotation lands on the same page region at ratio 1 and at ratio 2.

actor_type.description: Who acted (docs/EVENTS.md section 5). Actor identity is never inferred from display text alone, and the distinction between human_user and agent_session is what the acceptance authority rules of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15 are decided on.

actor.description: The actor of an event or a write. The type is always present, because an authority rule that depends on it must never fall back to a default.

id.description: Identifier of the acting principal, where one exists.

display.description: Human-readable label. Never used to establish identity.

review_priority.description: How urgently a review should be worked (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14). It orders a queue and never gates a transition: an urgent review and a routine one obey the same lifecycle and the same authority rules.

finding_source.description: Whether a human or an agent authored the finding. It is recorded on the first row rather than derived later, because the acceptance authority rule depends on it for the life of the finding. It is derived by the control plane from the authenticated actor and is never a field a caller may supply: a client able to set it could forge a human-authored finding, or relabel its own to escape the rule that a human decides.

annotation_type.description: Annotation shape (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16). All six types of that section are carried. freehand carries a sampled path beside the bounding box every other box type carries, so a reader that cannot draw the path still knows the region the mark covers (ADR-0032).

artefact_state.description: Whether the artefact may be treated as evidence. Only available has been verified against the declared size and digest (docs/API.md section 15).

redaction_state.description: Redaction applied to the stored bytes (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 20, docs/SECURITY.md section 14). Stage 0 records the state and runs no redaction, so an operator can tell an unredacted artefact from a redacted one rather than assuming.

retention_class.description: Retention bucket the artefact belongs to (docs/SECURITY.md section 14). Stage 0 stores the classification and runs no expiry job.

verification_status.description: Status of a verification submission (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19).

message_type.description: Version 1 event type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored. This enumeration MUST equal the keys of x-protocol.messages.

error_class.description: Stable refusal code, drawn from the docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12 enumeration so a refusal reaches an agent with the same code the HTTP API reports. This enumeration MUST equal x-protocol.error_classes.

viewport.description: Browser viewport in CSS pixels plus the device pixel ratio (docs/API.md section 11). Recorded on a finding so the capture can be reproduced at the size it was seen at.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio the capture was taken at.

scroll_position.description: Document scroll offset in CSS pixels at capture time. Without it a viewport-sized screenshot cannot be placed back on the page it came from.

content_rectangle.description: The reference frame for every normalised coordinate: the intrinsic pixel extent of the stored image, origin at its top-left (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16). A renderer converts once, at the edge, from this rectangle to whatever box it is drawing into; mixing CSS pixels, device pixels, the rendered element box and the intrinsic size is the usual cause of a misplaced overlay.

width_px.description: Intrinsic width of the stored image in device pixels.

height_px.description: Intrinsic height of the stored image in device pixels.

css_pixel_box.description: A rectangle in CSS pixels within the captured document, used only inside element context. Annotation geometry is never expressed this way.

annotation_path_point.description: One sampled point of a freehand path, normalised to the artefact content rectangle exactly as every other geometry member is. A path is a list of these rather than a string of drawing commands, because a command string is a second grammar to validate and an SVG path is a place to hide markup (ADR-0032).

annotation_geometry.description: Normalised geometry in the exact shape of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16, extended with the head of an arrow, an optional rotation and the sampled path of a freehand mark. Every member lies between 0 and 1 inclusive against the artefact content rectangle. Which members a type requires is fixed by x-protocol.vocabularies.geometry_by_annotation_type and enforced by checkGeometryForType, because JSON Schema cannot condition a nested object on the sibling type property.

x.description: Left edge for a box, position for a point or marker, tail for an arrow.

y.description: Top edge for a box, position for a point or marker, tail for an arrow.

width.description: Box width. Required for rectangle and ellipse, forbidden for the other types.

height.description: Box height. Required for rectangle and ellipse, forbidden for the other types.

x2.description: Arrow head, horizontal. Required for arrow, forbidden for the other types.

y2.description: Arrow head, vertical. Required for arrow, forbidden for the other types.

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation of a box about its own centre, in turns rather than degrees, so that this member obeys the same 0 to 1 bound as every other one and docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16 keeps a single range rule. 0.25 is a quarter turn. Optional for rectangle and ellipse, forbidden for the other types; absent means unrotated.

path.description: Sampled points of a freehand stroke, in drawing order, each normalised to the artefact content rectangle. Required for freehand, forbidden for the other types. The bound is 128 points: a stroke is decimated by the client that drew it, and an unbounded path would be a way to make one annotation cost more than the finding it belongs to.

element_context.description: Optional semantic link to the element under the geometry (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 17). Selectors are hints, not permanent identity; reproduction must tolerate a changed DOM. Stage 0 stores what a caller supplies and computes nothing.

selector.description: Selector that located the element. Page-derived and untrusted.

text_excerpt.description: Bounded excerpt of the element's text. Page-derived and untrusted: displayed as text and never followed as instructions (ADR-0010).

bounding_box_css_pixels.description: Element box in CSS pixels at capture time.

dom_fingerprint.description: Digest of the element's structure, so a later reproduction can tell that the DOM changed.

review.description: A named review: the durable collaboration package and the system of record (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14, ADR-0004). organisation_id and project_id are present on the record itself for defence-in-depth filtering (section 3).

slug.description: Project-scoped alias, unique among active reviews of this project.

description.description: Instruction to the agent that will resolve the review.

priority.description: How urgently the review should be worked. Ordering only; it gates nothing.

assigned_user_id.description: Human the review is assigned to, where one is.

assigned_agent_session_id.description: Agent session the review is assigned to or claimed by, where one is.

reopen_count.description: How many times the review has been reopened after acceptance. It is on the record because reopening preserves prior history rather than replacing it (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14), so the count is the only thing that distinguishes a first acceptance from a later one.

captured_branch.description: Branch the findings were captured from.

captured_commit.description: Commit the findings were captured from.

captured_workspace_id.description: Workspace the captured application was running in.

source_browser_session_id.description: Browser session the review was captured from. The review outlives it (ADR-0004); the reference records where it came from.

updated_at.description: Time of the last accepted mutation.

closed_at.description: Time the review reached a terminal status.

finding.description: One actionable unit inside a review (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15), carrying the captured context of docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 9 that makes it reproducible after the browser session has gone.

title.description: Short statement of what is wrong.

description.description: Detail a reader needs in order to reproduce and judge the finding.

source.description: Whether a human or an agent authored the finding. A human-authored finding can only be finally accepted by a human.

url.description: URL the finding was captured at.

viewport.description: Viewport and device pixel ratio at capture time.

scroll_position.description: Document scroll offset at capture time.

captured_commit.description: Commit the capture was taken from.

screenshot_artefact_id.description: Verified original screenshot the annotations are placed on. The original is immutable and stored apart from the overlay records (ADR-0006).

element_context.description: Element the geometry refers to, where the caller resolved one.

acceptance_criteria.description: What a resolution has to demonstrate.

updated_at.description: Time of the last accepted mutation.

annotation.description: Structured geometry over an original artefact (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16). It references the artefact rather than being drawn into it, which is what makes it editable, queryable and renderable at any size (ADR-0006).

artefact_id.description: Original artefact the geometry is normalised against.

geometry.description: Normalised geometry against the artefact content rectangle.

geometry_version.description: Version of the member list this geometry was written against, taken from x-protocol.vocabularies.geometry_by_annotation_type for the annotation's own type. Derived by the control plane from the type and never supplied by a caller: a stored geometry has to say which rule it obeyed, and a client able to name it could claim a member list its geometry does not satisfy (ADR-0032).

label.description: Text alternative for the mark, required by docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 19 so the annotation list conveys the same information as the canvas.

marker_number.description: Ordinal shown inside a numbered marker.

style_hint.description: Advisory emphasis. A renderer that ignores it still produces a correct overlay, so it can never carry meaning that only appears visually.

revision.description: Revision of this annotation. An edit records a new revision and retains the previous one (docs/API.md section 14).

deleted_at.description: When the annotation was withdrawn. The row is retained; the current projection hides it.

artefact.description: Metadata for binary evidence stored outside PostgreSQL (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 20). PostgreSQL is authoritative for availability: only a verified artefact is evidence.

state.description: Whether the artefact may be treated as evidence.

storage_key.description: Content-addressed key. Absent until the bytes are stored.

content_type.description: Media type of the stored bytes.

size_bytes.description: Byte length the server verified. Absent until verification succeeds.

sha256.description: Digest the server recomputed from the stored bytes. Absent until verification succeeds.

content_rectangle.description: Intrinsic pixel extent of an image artefact, which is the frame annotation geometry is normalised against.

redaction_state.description: Redaction applied to the stored bytes.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session the capture came from, where there was one.

created_at.description: When the upload intent was recorded.

available_at.description: When verification succeeded and the artefact became evidence.

expires_at.description: When retention becomes due for the artefact, computed from retention_class at intent. Stage 1 records it and runs no deletion, so a reader must treat it as the date after which the artefact MAY be removed rather than as a promise that it has been.

disposition.description: How the bytes are served. Derived from content_type by the server and never chosen by a caller.

encryption_key_reference.description: Identifier of the key that would decrypt the stored bytes, held apart from the ciphertext (docs/SECURITY.md section 15). Application-layer envelope encryption is a later stage: Stage 1 stores this field, writes nothing into it by default, and encrypts nothing. A null value therefore means the bytes are not application-encrypted, which is what an operator relying on volume encryption needs to be able to see.

source_artefact_id.description: Artefact this one was derived from, for a thumbnail. The original is never rewritten to carry its derivative (ADR-0006).

thumbnail_state.description: What became of this artefact's derived thumbnail.

thumbnail_artefact_id.description: The generated thumbnail, once one exists. It is a separate artefact with its own digest, not a variant of this one.

deleted_at.description: When the artefact was deleted. The metadata row is retained so the audit trail still resolves the identifier; the bytes are gone and no grant may be minted.

encryption_key_reference.description: Opaque reference to a key held in an external key manager. It is a reference and never key material: docs/SECURITY.md section 15 requires key identifiers to be stored separately from ciphertext, and an event or an API response carrying the key itself would defeat that.

artefact_upload_intent_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/artefacts/uploads (docs/API.md section 15). It declares what is about to be uploaded; every value in it is a claim the server verifies against the stored bytes before the artefact becomes evidence. Nothing here reaches the storage key, which is derived from the digest the server itself computes (ADR-0012).

kind.description: What the bytes are. The kind fixes which media types are accepted, so a DOM snapshot cannot be uploaded as a screenshot.

content_type.description: Declared media type. A claim: the leading bytes are the evidence, and a mismatch is refused on upload.

sha256.description: Declared digest of the bytes about to be uploaded.

retention_class.description: Retention bucket, which fixes expires_at. Defaults to the class for the kind when absent.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session the capture came from, where there was one.

source_artefact_id.description: Artefact this one is derived from, for a thumbnail.

filename.description: Display metadata only. It never reaches the storage key, and a value that is a path rather than a name is refused.

filename_label.description: A display filename: a name, never a path. The storage key is content-addressed, so traversal through this value is structurally impossible (ADR-0012); it is refused anyway, because a stored ../../etc/passwd is a value some later exporter might join to a directory (docs/TESTING.md section 10). The pattern admits no separator and no leading dot; the further rule that a name may not contain a doubled dot is enforced in code, because a negative lookahead is not portable to every language this package generates.

artefact_upload_intent_response.description: Result of an upload intent (docs/API.md section 15 step 2). upload_path is the proxied endpoint the filesystem driver serves; upload_url is the short-lived presigned target the s3 driver may return instead. Exactly one is present, so an uploader does not have to know which driver the deployment runs.

artefact_id.description: Artefact the intent created. It is pending: not evidence, and no grant may be minted for it.

upload_path.description: Server-relative path to POST the bytes to. It is returned under both drivers, because Stage 1 proxies the upload under both: the server is where content-type validation happens, so no byte reaches storage before it passes.

upload_url.description: Absolute short-lived presigned URL to PUT the bytes to. It is scoped to this one object and expires; it is never a durable public URL. ADR-0012 permits the s3 driver to issue one and Stage 1 does not: both drivers proxy the upload so that content-type validation happens before any byte is stored, so this member is reserved and never present today.

upload_expires_at.description: When a presigned upload target stops working.

max_bytes.description: Largest body this deployment accepts, so an uploader can refuse locally rather than discovering the bound halfway through a transfer.

artefact_upload_completion_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/artefacts/:artefactId/complete (docs/API.md section 15 step 4). The observed values are what the uploader believes it sent; the server compares them with the intent and, decisively, with the bytes it reads back out of the store.

sha256.description: Digest the uploader observed over the bytes it sent.

artefact_resource.description: The artefact://<artefact-id> and screenshot://<artefact-id> resource representation (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 8). Browser-derived bytes are untrusted input, so the representation carries the trust label and the instruction policy on every read (ADR-0010); an agent that finds instructions in a DOM snapshot has found page content, not a command.

state.description: Only available may be treated as evidence.

content_type.description: Media type of the stored bytes.

sha256.description: Digest the control plane verified, which is what ties a claim about the picture to the bytes.

content_rectangle.description: Intrinsic pixel extent of an image artefact.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session the capture came from.

redaction_state.description: Redaction applied to the stored bytes.

disposition.description: How the bytes are served if fetched.

content_path.description: Path that serves the bytes for the grant minted by this read. It is not a credential: the caller must still authenticate as the grant's subject (ADR-0019).

degraded.description: Present when the client could not be given what it asked for and was given something usable instead. Its absence means the read was complete.

trust.description: Trust label for the content (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13). Uploaded artefact bytes are untrusted.

instruction_policy.description: What the agent must do with any instruction-shaped text it finds in the content: not follow it.

artefact_resource_degradation.description: Why a resource read returned less than it was asked for, in the shape docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 18 requires of every failure state: a stable reason and a sentence saying what the caller still has. A degraded read is a success — the alternative, failing a screenshot read because the client cannot display images, would deny the agent the digest and the metadata it can use.

reason.description: Stable cause. image_resources_unsupported is the client capability of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.3 and docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 18; active_content_not_inlined is a DOM snapshot, whose bytes are only ever served as an attachment.

detail.description: What the caller was given instead, in words an agent can relay to a human.

artefact_store_status.description: Artefact-store figures for reviewplane status (docs/OPERATIONS.md section 3). The byte totals are what PostgreSQL records as verified, not what the driver reports on disk: metadata is authoritative for availability (ADR-0012), and a driver total would also count bytes belonging to a deleted artefact whose key is still shared.

available.description: Whether the driver answered a round-trip probe. False means uploads will be refused and existing evidence cannot be read.

detail.description: Why the driver is unavailable, when it is.

artefact_count.description: Verified artefacts that have not been deleted.

stored_bytes.description: Bytes those artefacts occupy, counting each content-addressed key once. Two artefacts with identical bytes share one stored object, so summing per artefact would overstate the volume an operator has to back up.

pending_bytes.description: Bytes declared by intents that have not completed verification. They are not evidence and may never become any.

artefact_deleted.description: Payload of artefact.deleted. Deletion is an audited access-class event (docs/SECURITY.md section 16): the identifier stays resolvable in the audit trail after the bytes are gone.

sha256.description: Digest of the bytes that were removed, where the artefact had been verified.

size_bytes.description: Byte length of the deleted artefact.

bytes_removed.description: Whether the stored object was removed. False when another live artefact shares the same content-addressed key: keys are derived from content, so identical bytes are one object, and removing it would take evidence that is still referenced.

reason.description: Why the artefact was deleted, where the caller gave one.

artefact_thumbnail_generated.description: Payload of artefact.thumbnail_generated. The thumbnail is a separate artefact with its own digest and its own verification: the original is never rewritten (ADR-0006).

artefact_id.description: Source artefact the job ran for.

state.description: Outcome recorded on the source artefact.

thumbnail_artefact_id.description: The generated thumbnail, when one was produced.

content_rectangle.description: Intrinsic pixel extent of the thumbnail.

reason.description: Why no thumbnail was produced, for the unsupported and failed outcomes.

verification_reference.description: A pointer to a verification submission and the before and after evidence it rests on (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). Stage 0 stores and serves the reference; submission and human acceptance are Stage 1, but the shape is fixed now so an agent's evidence has somewhere to land.

submitted_by.description: Actor that submitted it. An agent may submit; only a human may accept a human-authored finding.

summary.description: What was changed and how it was checked.

branch.description: Branch the fix was made on.

commit.description: Commit the fix was made in.

after_artefact_id.description: Artefact showing the state after the fix. A completion claim without one is refused with EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

tested_viewports.description: Viewports the fix was checked at. AGENTS.md requires UI-facing work to be checked at 390x844 and 1440x900 at minimum, and this is where the claim to have done so is recorded.

checks.description: Checks the submitter claims to have performed.

artefact_ids.description: Every artefact the submission rests on, in submission order. The server has already verified that each belongs to this project and to a browser session of this project before the event is written; evidence from elsewhere never reaches this list.

supersedes_verification_id.description: The verification this one replaced as the current claim, where there was one. The earlier record is marked superseded rather than deleted, so a finding carries the whole history of what was claimed about it across reopen cycles (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19).

superseded_by_verification_id.description: The verification that replaced this one. Present only where status is superseded.

superseded_at.description: When this record stopped being the current claim.

error_details.description: Machine-readable detail for a refusal. Bounded rather than free-form, so a refusal cannot become a channel for arbitrary content.

current_version.description: Version the record actually holds, returned with VERSION_CONFLICT.

field.description: Path of the offending field, where one field is at fault.

missing_context.description: Captured-context fields a rejected finding lacked (docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 9).

required_evidence.description: Evidence a completion claim must carry, returned with EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

items.description: Name of a missing piece of evidence.

allowed_transitions.description: The transitions this actor may make from the current status, as from:to labels, returned with a refused transition (docs/API.md section 5). A refusal that only says no makes a caller guess, and a guessing agent retries.

reason.description: Why, where one code covers several causes (docs/API.md section 5).

retry_after_ms.description: How long to wait before retrying, returned with RATE_LIMITED.

domain_error.description: The docs/API.md section 5 error object. The code is the stable vocabulary of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12; the message is for a human and is never parsed.

review_create_request.description: Creates a named review inside a project. The captured source context is required, because a review that cannot say which branch, commit, workspace and session it came from cannot be judged against a later state of the code.

description.description: Instruction to the agent that will resolve the review.

status.description: Initial status. Defaults to DRAFT; only DRAFT and READY may be requested at creation.

priority.description: How urgently the review should be worked. Defaults to medium.

captured_branch.description: Branch the findings were captured from.

captured_commit.description: Commit the findings were captured from.

captured_workspace_id.description: Workspace the captured application was running in.

source_browser_session_id.description: Browser session the review was captured from.

review_update_request.description: Updates a review. expected_version is mandatory: a collaborative record with two writers needs the refusal more than it needs the convenience.

expected_version.description: Version the caller last read. A mismatch is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT and the current version in the details.

review_assign_request.description: Assigns a review to a human or to an agent session. Exactly one of the two is named: a review owned by both would leave the question the assignment exists to answer unanswered, and clearing an assignment is done by naming neither.

assigned_user_id.description: Human to assign the review to.

assigned_agent_session_id.description: Agent session to assign the review to.

reason.description: Why, recorded on the event.

review_transition_request.description: Body of the review lifecycle routes: request-review, accept, reopen and archive (docs/API.md section 12). The target status is fixed by the route rather than named in the body, so a caller cannot ask one route for another route's transition.

reason.description: Why, recorded on the event so an auditor reads a decision rather than a status. Required for reopen: a review returned for more work without a statement of what is wrong is an instruction nobody can act on (ADR-0036).

finding_claim_request.description: Claims one finding. The claim carries the same expected_version as any other write, so a human and an agent claiming at once produce one claim and one VERSION_CONFLICT rather than two silent overwrites.

finding_transition_request.description: Body of the human-only finding disposition routes: accept, reopen and wont-fix (docs/API.md section 13). Each is refused for an agent actor in the domain layer with AUTHORISATION_DENIED, whatever credential reached the route.

verification_id.description: The verification the decision is about: the one the deciding human was shown, not the one that happens to be current when the request arrives (ADR-0035). Required where the finding holds a current verification, and refused with VERSION_CONFLICT where it names one that has since been superseded, so evidence swapped under a reviewer cannot be accepted by a client that re-read the record before sending.

reason.description: Why the decision was made. Required for wont-fix and for reopen, because waiving or returning a reported problem without a reason is not a decision anybody can review later (ADR-0036).

duplicate_of_finding_id.description: The finding this one duplicates, where the disposition is DUPLICATE.

verification_create_request.description: Body of POST /api/v1/findings/:findingId/verifications (docs/API.md section 13). There is no submitted_by field and no status field, and their absence is the point: the submitter is derived from the authenticated actor and the status is always submitted, so no caller can forge an attribution or record a decision. Accepting or rejecting a verification is a human decision recorded on separate routes.

expected_version.description: Version the caller last read, where it wants the submission refused if the finding moved. Checked inside the transaction that writes the new version.

summary.description: What was changed and how it was checked. Stored and rendered as text, never as markup.

branch.description: Branch the fix was made on.

commit.description: Commit the fix was made in. It MUST differ from the commit the finding was captured at.

tested_viewports.description: Viewports the fix was checked at.

checks.description: Checks the submitter claims to have performed. They are recorded as that actor's claims and never as control-plane verification.

artefact_ids.description: Evidence. Each must exist, be available, and belong to this project; at least one must be a screenshot.

comment_create_request.description: Appends a comment to a review or a finding. There is no author field: attribution is derived from the authenticated actor, because a caller able to name its own actor type could make an agent's note read as a human's (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 18).

body.description: Comment text. Rendered as text and never as markup.

comment_update_request.description: Edits a comment. The edit appends a new revision and retains the previous one, so the history a reader needs to judge a changed instruction is never lost.

body.description: Replacement text, recorded as the next revision.

finding_create_request.description: Creates a finding inside a review. Every field of the docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 9 captured-context list is required except element context, which the flow itself marks as best effort; a request missing one is refused rather than stored incomplete.

title.description: Short statement of what is wrong.

description.description: Detail a reader needs to reproduce and judge the finding.

url.description: URL the finding was captured at.

viewport.description: Viewport and device pixel ratio at capture time.

scroll_position.description: Document scroll offset at capture time.

captured_commit.description: Commit the capture was taken from.

screenshot_artefact_id.description: Verified original screenshot. It must be available, in the same project, before a finding may reference it.

element_context.description: Element the geometry refers to, where the caller resolved one. Stage 0 stores it and computes nothing.

acceptance_criteria.description: What a resolution has to demonstrate.

annotations.description: Annotations to record with the finding, in one transaction, so a finding and the geometry that explains it never exist apart.

finding_update_request.description: Updates a finding. The status transition is checked against the authority rules of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15 before anything is written.

resolution_note.description: What was done, recorded with a transition towards resolution.

verification_id.description: The verification a human decision is about, where the requested status is a final disposition or a reopen and the finding holds a current claim (ADR-0035). The rule lives below the transport, so it is the same rule the dedicated disposition routes obey; this member is what lets a caller satisfy it here rather than being told to use another route.

reason.description: Why the decision was made, where the requested status is a final disposition or a reopen. Required for wont-fix and for reopen (ADR-0036).

annotation_create_request.description: Records one annotation against a finding's original screenshot. Geometry is validated against 0 to 1 inclusive at this boundary and refused when it falls outside, never clamped.

artefact_id.description: Original artefact the geometry is normalised against. It must be the finding's screenshot.

geometry.description: Normalised geometry against the artefact content rectangle.

label.description: Text alternative for the mark. Required, because the annotation list is an equal alternative to the canvas rather than a fallback.

annotation_update_request.description: Body of PATCH /api/v1/annotations/:annotationId (docs/API.md section 14). An edit records a new revision and retains the one it supersedes, so this request never overwrites anything. The annotation's type and artefact are not editable: changing either would make the retained revisions a history of two different marks, and the honest way to move a mark to another shape or another screenshot is to withdraw it and record a new one.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller read. An edit against a superseded revision is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT rather than applied, so two simultaneous edits produce one new revision and one refusal instead of a forked history.

geometry.description: Replacement geometry, validated against the annotation's existing type. Absent leaves the geometry as it was.

label.description: Replacement text alternative. Absent leaves the label as it was.

marker_number.description: Replacement ordinal for a numbered marker. Absent leaves it as it was.

style_hint.description: Replacement advisory emphasis. Absent leaves it as it was.

previous_slug.description: Slug replaced, where this was a rename.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

finding_annotated.description: Payload of finding.annotated. It is recorded for the first revision of an annotation and for every later one, so an edit and a withdrawal leave the same kind of trail a creation does; the revision on the annotation says which of the three it was, and a withdrawn revision carries deleted_at.

source.description: Who authored the finding, recorded on the transition so the authority rule that permitted it is legible in the audit trail.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

comment.description: One chronological discussion item on a review or on one of its findings (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 18). finding_id is absent for a comment on the review itself. Comments are append-only; the actor type is always explicit, because a reader must be able to tell an agent's note from a human's without inferring it from the wording, and it is derived from the authenticated actor rather than supplied.

review_id.description: Review the comment belongs to, directly or through its finding.

finding_id.description: Finding the comment is on. Absent when the comment is on the review itself.

body.description: Comment text. Rendered as text and never as markup.

created_by.description: Who wrote it, derived from the authenticated actor and never from the request body.

revision.description: Revision of the comment. Editing records a new revision and retains the previous one.

supersedes_comment_id.description: The revision this one replaces, where it is an edit. The replaced row survives: an edit appends, it does not overwrite.

superseded_at.description: When a later revision replaced this one. A revision carrying it is history rather than the current text.

inbox_item_status.description: Inbox-item status (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 21). acknowledged and completed are separate values because receipt and completion are separate facts, and a single value covering both would make the audit question unanswerable.

inbox_item_type.description: Why an inbox item exists. review_assigned is created when a review is assigned; finding_reopened is created when a human reopens a finding.

inbox_item_recipient_type.description: What kind of principal an inbox item was delivered to. It is the actor vocabulary narrowed to the two that can hold work: a system or an integration receives nothing.

inbox_item.description: A durable work notification (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 21). It exists so an agent learns what a human wants changed by retrieving a record rather than by guessing, and so a human can see whether the delivery was received. It names the work and never carries it: a review reference and a count, not the review's contents.

project_id.description: Owning project. An inbox item never crosses one.

recipient_type.description: What kind of principal it was delivered to.

recipient_id.description: The principal it was delivered to. Absent for an item addressed to whoever picks the project's work up next.

title.description: What a human called the work.

review_id.description: Review the item is about, where there is one.

finding_id.description: Finding the item is about, for a reopened finding.

priority.description: Priority of the work. It orders a queue and gates nothing.

finding_count.description: Findings in the referenced review when the item was created.

assigned_by.description: Who caused the item, derived from the authenticated actor.

completed_at.description: When the work was recorded complete.

expires_at.description: When the item stops being current work, where an expiry was set.

recipient_type.description: What kind of principal it was delivered to.

recipient_id.description: The principal it was delivered to, where one was named.

status.description: Status at creation, which is pending.

review_id.description: Review the item is about, where there is one.

finding_id.description: Finding the item is about, where there is one.

finding_count.description: Findings in the referenced review at creation.

inbox_item_acknowledged.description: Payload of inbox_item.acknowledged. It carries no completion member, because acknowledgement is not completion and a payload that could express both would invite a consumer to treat them as one.

previous_status.description: Status the item was actually in, read under the lock that changed it.

review_id.description: Review the item is about, where there is one.

previous_status.description: Status the item was actually in.

review_id.description: Review the item is about, where there is one.

previous_status.description: Status the item was actually in.

review_id.description: Review the item is about, where there is one.

reason.description: Why it was dismissed, where the caller supplied one.

previous_status.description: Status the item was actually in.

review_id.description: Review the item is about, where there is one.

verification_checks.description: The checks a verification claims to have performed (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). They are recorded as claims and are never proof on their own: the artefacts are the evidence, and a human decides.

reproduced_before.description: Whether the defect was reproduced before anything was changed.

console_errors_reviewed.description: Whether console output was reviewed after the change.

network_failures_reviewed.description: Whether failed network requests were reviewed after the change.

accessibility_checked.description: Whether keyboard navigation and visible focus were checked.

previous_claimed_by.description: Actor that held the claim before, where a claim was taken over.

comment.description: The comment as recorded. It carries no finding_id, because it is on the review itself.

assigned_user_id.description: Human it was assigned to, where it was.

assigned_agent_session_id.description: Agent session it was assigned to, where it was.

previous_assigned_user_id.description: Human it was assigned to before, where one held it.

previous_assigned_agent_session_id.description: Agent session it was assigned to before, where one held it.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

accepted_by.description: The human who decided. The type is always human_user: an agent reaching this event is not representable, because the domain layer refuses the transition before the event is written.

finding_count.description: Findings the review held when it was accepted.

human_finding_count.description: How many of those a human authored. Acceptance rests on every one of them having reached a final disposition, so the count is recorded rather than left to be recomputed against a table that has since moved on.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

reopen_count.description: How many times this review has now been reopened. Prior findings, evidence and comments are retained, so the count is what distinguishes one acceptance cycle from the next.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

from.description: Status it was archived from. Archival is not deletion: the findings, evidence and events all outlive it.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

disposition.description: The final disposition reached: RESOLVED, WONT_FIX or DUPLICATE.

source.description: Who authored the finding, recorded here because it is the input the authority rule of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15 was decided on.

decided_by.description: The human who decided. Stage 1 enables no policy that would let anything else reach this event.

duplicate_of_finding_id.description: The finding this one duplicates, where the disposition is DUPLICATE.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one. Required by the route for WONT_FIX.

review_id.description: Review the transition was requested on.

code.description: The stable refusal code the caller was answered with.

reason.description: Short explanation, drawn from the refusal rather than from the request.

finding_id.description: Finding the transition was requested on.

source.description: Who authored the finding. It is the input the authority rule was decided on, so a reader can see why the refusal happened without re-deriving it.

code.description: The stable refusal code the caller was answered with.

reason.description: Short explanation, drawn from the refusal rather than from the request.

verification_count.description: Verifications the finding already holds. Reopening preserves prior verification history (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15), so the count says what was kept rather than implying a fresh start.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

finding_verification_submitted.description: Payload of finding.verification_submitted. It carries the whole claim, and beside it the finding and the version that finding holds after the submission, so an auditor can order a claim against the status changes around it without a second read (docs/EVENTS.md section 7).

verification.description: The verification as submitted, with status submitted.

finding_id.description: Finding the claim concerns, at the top level so a consumer filtering one finding's timeline need not open the claim to decide whether the event belongs to it.

version.description: Version the finding holds after the submission.

supersedes_verification_id.description: The verification this submission replaced as the current claim, where there was one. Supersession is recorded on the submission that caused it rather than as an event of its own, in the same way an edited comment is recorded as another comment_added carrying a back-reference: one act, one occurrence.

finding_verification_accepted.description: Payload of finding.verification_accepted. It names the verification a human accepted, which finding.resolved does not: a trail recording that somebody resolved a finding without recording which claim they were looking at cannot answer the one question an auditor asks after an evidence swap (RVP-93, ADR-0035).

verification_id.description: The verification accepted. It is the identifier the deciding client rendered its comparison from, and the control plane refused the decision unless it was still the current claim.

submitted_by.description: The actor that submitted the claim, recorded beside the actor that accepted it so the authority boundary is readable from one event.

decided_by.description: The human who accepted. Nothing that is not a human_user can reach this event.

after_artefact_id.description: The after screenshot the accepted claim rested on, where it had one.

version.description: Version the finding holds after the decision.

reason.description: Why, where the caller supplied one.

finding_verification_rejected.description: Payload of finding.verification_rejected. A reopen is a rejection of a specific claim, and naming it is what keeps a repeatedly-reopened finding legible: the record says which evidence failed rather than only that the finding came back (RVP-93, ADR-0035).

verification_id.description: The verification rejected. The record itself is retained with status rejected; nothing about a rejection deletes evidence.

submitted_by.description: The actor whose claim was rejected.

version.description: Version the finding holds after the decision.

reason.description: Why the claim was rejected. Required: a reopen with no statement of what is still wrong is work an agent cannot act on (ADR-0036).

evidence_assurance.description: Who established each piece of evidence (ADR-0031). A surface that reports evidence MUST NOT merge the two lists: the first names checks this control plane performed, the second names claims the submitting actor made and nothing confirmed. A reviewer shown one undifferentiated list of ticks would accept a machine agreeing with itself, which is the confusion the product exists to remove.

verified_by_control_plane.description: What the control plane checked for itself before recording the verification.

asserted_by_agent.description: What the submitter claimed and nothing confirmed. Empty is a truthful answer.

asserted_by.description: The actor whose claim the assertions are. Absent where there is no verification to attribute them to, because naming an actor with no claims behind it would attribute something to somebody.

verification_review.description: One verification as a human reviewer reads it: the claim, the assurance split of docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 13, and the qualifications on the claim that are worth saying but not worth refusing. It is served by GET /api/v1/findings/:findingId/verifications/:verificationId so a comparison is rendered from a named claim rather than from whatever is latest at render time (ADR-0035).

verification.description: The claim, as recorded. Its summary is untrusted human-facing content and MUST be rendered as text (ADR-0010).

assurance.description: What the control plane checked, and separately what the submitter asserted.

warnings.description: Qualifications on the claim: a defect not reproduced first, an unchecked accessibility pass, a branch no workspace corroborates. They are statements about the evidence rather than claims attributed to the submitter, so they are not in the asserted list.

is_current.description: Whether this claim is still the one a decision may be taken on. False for a superseded or already-decided record, which a reviewer may read but may not accept.

completion_result.description: The result of the completion gate (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.8). None of the four terminates the agent, and blocked_pending_review is a correct terminal answer for an agent rather than a failure to retry.

requirement_label.description: One outstanding requirement, composed by the control plane and written for a reader: 390x844 verification, after screenshot, console review. Nothing an agent supplied is echoed through it.

review_completion_evaluated.description: Payload of review.completion_evaluated. It records what an agent was told, not what changed: the result, the outstanding requirements and the agent's own account of what it believes it finished. The summary is the agent's claim and is stored inert — it is not evidence, it did not affect the result, and it MUST NOT be rendered as markup (docs/SECURITY.md section 18, ADR-0010).

finding_id.description: The single finding the evaluation was narrowed to, where it was.

missing.description: What was still outstanding when the gate ran. Empty is a truthful answer and never on its own a statement that the work was accepted.

finding_count.description: How many findings the evaluation covered.

summary.description: The agent's account of what it believes it finished. A claim, recorded beside the control plane's answer rather than instead of it.

declared_size_bytes.description: Size the uploader declared. It is a claim until the server verifies it.

sha256.description: Digest the server recomputed from the stored bytes.

storage_key.description: Content-addressed key the bytes were filed under.

redaction_state.description: Redaction state recorded for the stored bytes.

content_rectangle.description: Intrinsic pixel extent, for an image artefact.

reason.description: Why verification failed.

code.description: Stable code the caller was refused with.

artefact_id.description: Artefact the grant admits to, and only that one.

grant_id.description: Grant identifier. It appears in the content path and is not a credential on its own: the caller must still authenticate as the grant's subject.

subject.description: Principal the grant was minted for.

content_rectangle.description: Intrinsic pixel extent, which is the frame annotation geometry is normalised against.

viewport.description: Viewport the capture was taken at.

envelope.description: The docs/EVENTS.md section 2 event envelope. Every event names the organisation and project it belongs to, its position in that project's stream, and the actor that caused it; the payload schema is selected by type.

id.description: Event identifier, conventionally prefixed evt_. Consumers deduplicate on it.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema version. Stage 0 accepts 1 only; any other value is rejected rather than best-effort parsed.

sequence.description: Monotonic position within the project stream.

type.description: Version 1 event type. Unknown types are rejected.

project_id.description: Owning project. Every read of this stream is filtered by it.

actor.description: Actor that caused the change. Always explicit (docs/EVENTS.md section 5).

correlation.description: Identifiers linking the event to the work that produced it.

payload.description: Event payload. Its schema is selected by type. The event is bounded by x-protocol.limits.max_review_event_bytes and each payload by its own x-max-bytes.

correlation.description: Identifiers that link an event to the request, session and records it came from (docs/EVENTS.md section 2). It carries identifiers only: never a request body, a header or a credential (section 8).
